summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic systolic heart failure with an ejection fraction of 25%, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and productive cough. He presented with orthopnea and low oxygen saturation. Imaging revealed pulmonary edema and a right lung opacity suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with IV furosemide for heart failure exacerbation and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to levofloxacin for bacterial pneumonia. His respiratory status improved, and he became afebrile with resolving radiographic findings. Diuresis was paused due to rising creatinine, and he was discharged on oral furosemide with instructions to monitor weight and follow up on kidney function. Blood cultures and respiratory viral panels were negative.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
